meta.title: Terms of use — CarrierBridge
meta.description: Terms of use for the CarrierBridge service: account, subscriptions, obligations, liability, termination.

terms.intro: These terms govern access to carrier-bridge.com and use of the CarrierBridge service published by A2TL. Creating an account constitutes unreserved acceptance of them.

sections.title: 1. Purpose of the service
sections.body: CarrierBridge is software accessible online, intended for shippers. It allows transport rate sheets received as Excel files to be loaded while keeping their original structure, carrier offers to be compared for a given shipment, ancillary charges to be tracked, and energy indexation to be recalculated in order to identify any gaps with the amounts invoiced. The service is not intended for carriers.

sections.title: 2. User account
sections.body: Access to the service requires an account created with an email address and a password. The account holder is responsible for keeping their credentials confidential and for any action carried out from their account. They must inform the publisher without delay of any unauthorised use they become aware of.

sections.title: 3. Plans, subscriptions and payment
sections.body: The service is offered in several plans whose features and prices are set out on the Pricing page. Prices are shown excluding VAT, in euros. Paid subscriptions are billed at the frequency chosen at sign-up, monthly or annually. The Discovery plan is free and limited to the volumes stated on the Pricing page. Services charged per act — tenders, onboarding, connectors — are subject to a separate quotation or order.

sections.title: 4. Use of the service
sections.body: The user undertakes to import only documents they are entitled to hold and process, not to attempt to access other clients' data, not to disrupt the operation of the service, and not to extract content in bulk by automated means other than the API where it is included in their plan.

sections.title: 5. Client data and content
sections.body: Rate sheets, volumes, negotiated prices and imported documents remain the property of the client. The publisher does not disclose them to third parties, does not share them with other clients and does not pass them to carriers. They are processed solely to deliver the service, under the conditions described in the privacy policy.

sections.title: 6. Availability and changes
sections.body: The publisher takes reasonable steps to keep the service accessible. Interruptions may occur for maintenance, updates or external causes. The service evolves: features may be added, changed or withdrawn. Features identified as beta, in particular the assisted sourcing module, are provided as is, with no guarantee of results or of continued availability.

sections.title: 7. Nature of the results produced
sections.body: The price comparisons, indexation recalculations and gap alerts produced by the service are decision aids, calculated from the data supplied by the client and the parameters they have entered. They constitute neither legal advice, nor contractual analysis, nor certification that an invoice is correct or that a document is valid. It is for the client to check their contracts and to conduct their own discussions with their carriers.

sections.title: 8. Liability
sections.body: The publisher's liability can be engaged only where fault is proven and is limited to direct loss. It may not exceed the amounts paid by the client over the twelve months preceding the triggering event. The publisher is not responsible for the commercial decisions taken by the client, nor for the consequences of any inaccuracy in the data the client has imported or configured.

sections.title: 9. Term and termination
sections.body: The subscription runs for the period chosen and renews automatically unless terminated before the renewal date from the client area. Termination ends access to the service at the end of the current period. The client may export their data before that date. In the event of a serious breach of these terms, the publisher may suspend access after a formal notice has gone unanswered.

sections.title: 10. Changes to these terms
sections.body: These terms may be amended. Clients are informed of any substantial change by electronic means before it takes effect.

sections.title: 11. Governing law and jurisdiction
sections.body: These terms are governed by French law. Failing an amicable settlement, any dispute falls within the jurisdiction of the courts of [[VILLE_JURIDICTION]].

meta.title: Privacy policy — CarrierBridge
meta.description: Data collected, purposes, retention periods, hosting in Europe and how to exercise your rights.

privacy.intro: This policy describes the personal data processed in connection with the carrier-bridge.com website and the CarrierBridge service, the purposes of that processing, and how you can exercise your rights.

sections.title: Data controller
sections.body: A2TL, [[ADRESSE_SIEGE]]. Contact: contact@carrier-bridge.com.

sections.title: Data processed
sections.body:
Account data: email address, password in encrypted form, company name, and where you provide them your name, role and telephone number.
Service usage data: rate sheets, simulated shipments, indexation settings, imported documents. This content relates to your professional activity rather than your private life, but may contain personal data (the name of a contact at a carrier, for example).
Contact data: information submitted through the contact form.
Audience measurement: aggregated page-view statistics, with no cookie and no identifier allowing you to be recognised from one visit to the next.

sections.title: Purposes and legal bases
sections.body:
Delivering the service and managing the account: performance of the contract.
Billing and accounting obligations: legal obligation.
Responding to contact enquiries: pre-contractual step or legitimate interest.
Improving the service and measuring audience: legitimate interest, using a cookieless solution with no profiling.
Informing our clients about changes to the service: legitimate interest, with the option to opt out at any time.

sections.title: Recipients and processors
sections.body:
Your data is not sold, rented or disclosed to third parties for commercial purposes. It is never passed to carriers. It is accessible only to authorised staff at the publisher, and to the technical providers strictly necessary to run the service, acting as processors and bound by contract.
Processors: Netlify (website hosting), [[HEBERGEUR_APPLICATION]] (application hosting, European region), Resend (transactional email), Plausible (cookieless audience measurement), [[PRESTATAIRE_PAIEMENT]] (subscription payments).

sections.title: Where data is held
sections.body:
Two things need separating.
The carrier-bridge.com website is hosted by Netlify, Inc., a company established in the United States, and delivered through a global network. It processes only contact form submissions and aggregated, cookieless audience measurement.
Service data — your rate sheets, volumes, negotiated prices and account — is hosted within the European Union, in a European region of [[HEBERGEUR_APPLICATION]].
Both providers are established in the United States. Access from a third country therefore cannot be excluded, solely for operational and technical support purposes. Those transfers are covered by the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, together with the technical measures described in the Security section.

sections.title: Retention periods
sections.body:
Account data and imported content: for the duration of the contract, then [[DUREE_APRES_RESILIATION]] after termination, so that data can be recovered or exported.
Accounting records and invoices: ten years, in line with legal obligations.
Contact enquiries with no follow-up: three years from the last exchange.
Audience statistics: aggregated, with no individual data retained.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Access to production environments is restricted and logged. Passwords are stored as hashes and are never accessible in clear text.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You have rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability over data concerning you. You can exercise them by writing to contact@carrier-bridge.com. We respond within one month. If, having contacted us, you consider your rights are not being respected, you may lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority (CNIL), 3 place de Fontenoy, 75007 Paris.

meta.title: Cookie settings — CarrierBridge
meta.description: Which cookies are set on carrier-bridge.com, what they are for, and how to refuse them.

cookies.intro: A cookie is a file placed on your device when you visit a site. Our approach is simple: we use no advertising trackers and no profiling cookies. Refusing audience measurement changes nothing about how the site works.

rows.name: Strictly necessary cookies
rows.purpose: Keeping your session, remembering your cookie choice, form security.

rows.name: Audience measurement
rows.purpose: Aggregated page-view statistics, with no cookie, no persistent identifier and no tracking of a visitor across sites.
rows.consent: Can be refused at any time

manage.title: Change your choice
manage.body: You can accept or refuse audience measurement at any time using the buttons below. Your choice is kept on this device.

browser.title: Browser settings
browser.body: You can also configure your browser to block or delete cookies. Blocking strictly necessary cookies may stop some parts of the site working properly.
